v.rationale:
I ran all four suites and they pass (impl-1: 22, impl-2: 37, impl-3: 31, impl-4: 37). I read every added file and probed each implementation with throwaway tests, deleted afterwards.

impl-2 ranks first. It is the cleanest and most idiomatic: a FormRequest, createOrFirst, signature middleware that rejects an empty secret, job attributes, WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited, a receipt queued only after the transaction commits, MassPrunable with onOneServer, and a policy for admin access. It also checks for an unknown order before calling the provider. Its only real flaw: queue:retry on a failed event does nothing, even though the README recommends it.

impl-3 has the strongest tests: it runs a real database queue worker to prove increasing backoff, retries running out, the 10 requests/second limit and the overlap lock. It also re-checks the event status under a row lock. It ranks below impl-2 because of a broken OrderFactory (no user_id, so Order::factory()->create() fails), duplicate receipts when two different payment.succeeded events arrive for one order, a hard-coded USD fallback, and no onOneServer on the cleanup schedule.

impl-4 uses modern APIs well (FailOnException, retryUntil). But its receipt notification is not queued, so mail goes out synchronously inside the job, and a mail failure leaves the order paid with the event stuck in processing. It also calls the provider before looking up the order, and adds an over-engineered command that re-dispatches stuck events.

impl-1 is last. It accepts forged signatures when the secret isn't configured (confirmed with a probe). Unknown event types are silently marked processed. It validates inline in the controller instead of using a FormRequest, uses magic status strings instead of enums, uses the legacy queue traits, and has the thinnest tests.
